You said:You

In MY language learning app angular/ionic I have this game mode: But it's not really well adjusted the layout and the labels are overlaping some nodes. Suggest me a 3x improvement to make this more usable, and to look a bit nicer
Analyzed

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

The main problem isn't the visual style itself. It's the radial layout trying to fit too many nodes, labels and status indicators into a very small screen.

I would keep the circular/constellation concept because it gives your game mode a nice identity, but change how the categories are arranged.

My recommendation would be a 3x improvement without completely redesigning your game mode.

1. What I would change

1. Separate labels from nodes

Labels should never intersect icons or progress badges. Give each node a dedicated label area underneath it.

High priority

2. Reduce the visual noise

Reduce the glow intensity, use thinner connecting lines and make completed nodes visually distinct without adding too many overlapping badges.

3. Give the map more breathing room

Use more of the available screen height, slightly increase node spacing and avoid squeezing all ten categories around the centre.

2. My recommended layout: improved constellation

I'd keep your existing concept, but introduce three important changes:

  • Core Vocabulary becomes a proper anchor at the top.

  • Categories are arranged in a larger circular orbit with labels in dedicated positions.

  • Each node has a small, consistent progress indicator rather than floating badges that collide with other elements.

A particularly important implementation detail:

Avoid calculating label positions independently from node positions.

If you retain the radial design, create a single category-position model containing the node coordinates and label coordinates. This will make it much easier to adapt the layout to different screen widths.

For example:

TypeScript
interface CategoryNode {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  icon: string;
  angle: number;
  radius: number;
  progress: number;
  completed: boolean;
}

Use CSS transforms for positioning and reserve a separate bounding area for each label.

My final recommendation

I would actually consider two modes:

  • Explore map: Your existing constellation concept, improved and interactive.

  • Category overview: A clean grid/list like the example above, accessible through a toggle.

This gives users the fun of exploring a game world without sacrificing usability.

One more thing: I'd remove the admin instruction banner from the normal user experience entirely. Admin functionality should not occupy valuable space in the learning interface.
